title: Sales Enablement: Comprehensive Playbook — Positioning, Competitive Briefs, Decks, Pricing, Case Studies & Security FAQ
author: Ava Martinez
content:
Overview:
This playbook centralizes Redwood Inference sales artifacts for field reps and solutions engineers: core positioning and messaging, short competitive briefs, a recommended pitch-deck structure, pragmatic pricing guidance, two repeatable case studies, and a security FAQ tailored for prospects. Use these assets to shorten cycles, align GTM conversations with product capabilities, and reduce ramp time for new hires.

Positioning & Messaging (elevator + three value themes):
- Elevator pitch (30s): Redwood Inference is a developer-first inference platform that delivers predictable, low-latency, and cost-efficient LLM serving across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments — allowing engineering teams to ship LLM features without owning complex serving infrastructure.
- Value theme 1 — Predictable Production Performance: Emphasize latency SLOs, consistent throughput across modes, and autoscaling policies. Call out Dedicated pools for guaranteed throughput and private deployments for regulated workloads.
- Value theme 2 — Cost & Efficiency Controls: Explain batching, KV/prefix caching, and quantization recommendations that reduce per-token costs while preserving output quality. Reference Redwood Optimize as the toolkit for automated suggestions.
- Value theme 3 — Operational Confidence & Security: Unified observability (per-route dashboards, traces, regression alerts), rollout controls (canary/A-B/automatic fallbacks), and enterprise-ready compliance (KMS, audit logs, private control plane).

Messaging by persona:
- Engineering Lead: Focus on SDKs, runtime performance, predictable latency, and automated batching. Share benchmark snippets and API examples.
- Platform/Infra: Highlight deployment abstraction, routing policies, and capacity controls (reserved + burst).
- Security/Compliance: Surface on-prem/VPC options, KMS/HSM support, audit logging, and SOC2/CIS processes.
- Product/PM: Emphasize fast experimentation with model pinning, rollouts and integrated evals to prevent regressions.

Competitive Briefs (concise one-paragraph summaries + rebuttals):
- Cloud-managed endpoints (vendor X): Strength: broad model catalog. Redwood rebuttal: stronger production tooling + deterministic performance controls and cheaper unit economics for steady-state inference via Dedicated and Optimize recommendations.
- LLM API-only providers (vendor Y): Strength: simple developer experience. Redwood rebuttal: while similar ease-of-use is provided, Redwood adds predictable SLOs, private deployment and enterprise controls needed for regulated customers.
- Self-hosted inference runtimes (vendor Z): Strength: deep control. Redwood rebuttal: we match control via Private + Dedicated offerings while removing operational burden with a unified control plane and optional on-prem packaging.

Top competitive objections & suggested responses:
1) "We can build it ourselves." — Response: Outline 6–9 month effort and ongoing maintenance costs; present cost/latency tradeoffs and Redwood's reserved capacity and SLA benefits.
2) "Vendor lock-in concerns." — Response: Explain model/version portability, standard APIs, and data export paths.
3) "We need on-prem air-gapped deployments." — Response: Describe Redwood Private on-prem package and support model.

Pitch Deck: recommended slide order and talking points
1) Title & Hook — customer logo + one-line outcome (e.g., reduce inference cost 3x while meeting 99th%-ile latency target)
2) Problem Statement — pain of unpredictable latency, rising token costs, and ops burden
3) Why Redwood — three value themes + proof points (benchmarks, case results)
4) How it works (high-level) — serving runtime, smart routing, caching, and deployment modes (hosted/dedicated/private)
5) Demos & API examples — 2-minute live demo or synthetic request/response flow
6) Pricing Options & Recommended Fit — hosted pay-as-you-go, Dedicated commitments, Private licensing
7) Security & Compliance — SOC2, KMS, audit logs, network isolation options
8) Case Studies & Outcomes — before/after metrics
9) Implementation Plan & Timeline — 4–8 week pilot, success criteria, handoff model
10) Ask & Next Steps — POC proposal, stakeholders, and decision calendar

Pricing Guidance (field-friendly):
- Hosted (self-serve): usage-based per-token pricing tiers. Guidance: ideal for evaluation, early-stage customers, and unpredictable workloads. Offer trial credits and a 30-day pilot with limits.
- Dedicated (reserved): monthly/annual committed throughput. Guidance: recommended for production workloads >X tokens/day or >Y concurrent streams (define Y per rep using current capacity table). Include typical commitment sizes and uplift options for burst capacity.
- Private (enterprise license): platform fee + support tier and optional on-prem packaging. Guidance: price by node/cluster + support; include deployment and integration services as line items.
- Discounting guidance: follow negotiated deal levels: up to 15% for self-serve expansion, 15–35% for committed Dedicated contracts (scale by ARR and term), and custom pricing for Private depending on services.
- Packaging add-ons: advanced observability retention, compliance packages, premium SLA.

Quick pricing cheat-sheet (example figures for field use):
- Pilot: $0–10k (credits + 4–8 week POC)
- Small dedicated: $3k/mo (entry reserved pool)
- Mid-market: $15k–50k/mo (multi-GPU reserved capacity)
- Enterprise/private: custom (license + deployment services)
Note: use finance-approved price bands in CRM; contact pricing@redwood-inference.com for exceptions.

Case Studies (2 concise, repeatable templates):
1) FinServ Analytics Co. (anonymized):
- Problem: High-latency document parsing pipeline causing customer SLA misses.
- Solution: Migration to Redwood Dedicated with KV caching and quantized model variant for production.
- Outcome: 60% reduction in median latency, 3x throughput at 40% lower per-token cost. Pilot -> production in 6 weeks.
- Owner/Contacts: Solutions Engineering lead: Maya Singh.

2) Consumer SaaS Startup (anonymized):
- Problem: Rapidly increasing inference cost during growth phase.
- Solution: Hybrid routing (hosted fallback + dedicated core) + batching and Optimize recommendations.
- Outcome: 55% reduction in monthly inference costs while maintaining 95th%-ile latency SLOs.
- Owner/Contacts: Customer Success manager: Noah Patel.

Sales Playbook: typical 4-week pilot to production path
Week 0: Discovery & alignment — collect SLAs, workloads, and data sensitivity
Week 1: Pilot kickoff — sandbox credentials, baseline performance tests, pilot success criteria
Week 2–3: Iterate on prompt engineering, batching, and caching; collect cost/latency metrics
Week 4: Review outcomes and recommend Dedicated sizing or Private engagement
Handoff: Solutions Eng -> Customer Success for onboarding + quarterly QBR cadence

Security FAQ for Prospects (top questions with short answers):
Q: Do you offer on-prem or VPC deployment?
A: Yes. Redwood provides a Private deployment option (VPC and an on-prem package) for regulated customers.
Q: How is data protected in transit and at rest?
A: TLS 1.2+ in transit; at-rest encryption with customer-managed KMS options for Private deployments.
Q: Is customer data used to train models?
A: No. Customer data is not used to train Redwood models. For hosted API, we provide data handling contracts and opt-out controls per customer agreements.
Q: What compliance attestations do you have?
A: SOC2 Type II (control baseline), penetration testing annually, and support for customer audits. Contact compliance@redwood-inference.com for evidence requests.
Q: How are access controls and audit trails handled?
A: RBAC, SSO/SAML integrations, API keys with scoped permissions, and detailed audit logs available for Private and Dedicated customers.
Q: What is your incident response process?
A: We maintain documented incident runbooks, a postmortem process, and a customer notification SLA for Sev 1/2 incidents. See /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response for details.

1) Bookmark this page and link the deck to opportunities in CRM.
2) Use the "pilot checklist" and attach the recommended success criteria to proposals.
3) Route non-standard security requests to compliance@redwood-inference.com.

summary: Single-page sales enablement playbook covering messaging, competitive rebuttals, pitch deck flow, pricing guidance, case studies, and a security FAQ for prospect conversations.
